questions.title: Foundation: Build a random variable from a sample space
questions.prompt: A fair coin is tossed twice. Let $X$ be the number of heads observed. List the sample space, apply the rule $X$ to every outcome, state the support of $X$, and identify the event $\{X=1\}$.

steps.title: Write the outcomes
steps.body: $\Omega=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$. The experiment produces one of these four strings.

steps.title: Collect the possible values
steps.body: The support is $S_X=\{0,1,2\}$. Notice that the support contains numbers, not coin strings.

steps.title: Translate the requested event
steps.body: $\{X=1\}=\{HT,TH\}$, because those are exactly the outcomes containing one head.

questions.title: Developing: Classify counts and measurements
questions.prompt: For each variable, state whether it is discrete or continuous and justify the decision: (i) the number of support tickets received in an hour, (ii) the exact time between two ticket arrivals, (iii) the number of urgent tickets among the next 10, and (iv) the exact duration of a support call.

steps.title: Variable (i)
steps.body: Ticket arrivals are counted in whole numbers, so the number received is discrete.

steps.title: Variable (ii)
steps.body: Elapsed time is measured and may take any nonnegative real value, so it is continuous.

steps.title: Variable (iii)
steps.body: Urgent tickets are counted from 0 through 10, so the variable is discrete.

steps.title: Variable (iv)
steps.body: Call duration is measured on a time interval, so it is continuous.

steps.title: State the general rule
steps.body: Counts are discrete; measurements across intervals are continuous.

questions.title: Exam: Several random variables on one experiment
questions.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled and a stopwatch measures the exact time taken for the dice to stop. Define $X$ as the sum of the faces, $Y$ as the larger face, and $T$ as the measured stopping time. For the outcome $\left(2,5\right)$, find $X$ and $Y$, describe the event $\{X=7\}$, state the supports of $X$ and $Y$, and classify all three variables.

steps.title: Apply both rules
steps.body: For $\left(2,5\right)$, the sum is $X=2+5=7$, while the larger face is $Y=5$.

steps.title: Find the sum support
steps.body: The smallest sum is $2$, the largest is $12$, and every integer between them is possible: $S_X=\{2,3,\ldots,12\}$.

steps.title: Find the maximum support
steps.body: The larger die can be any integer from $1$ to $6$: $S_Y=\{1,2,\ldots,6\}$.

steps.title: Classify the variables
steps.body: $X$ and $Y$ are discrete because they take separated integer values. $T$ is continuous because exact stopping time is measured along an interval.

questions.answer: **Final answer.** $X=7$ and $Y=5$ for $\left(2,5\right)$; $X,Y$ are discrete, while $T$ is continuous.

questions.title: Foundation: Check a proposed PMF
questions.prompt: A discrete random variable has support $\{0,1,2,3\}$ and proposed masses $0.10,0.25,0.40,0.25$, respectively. Determine whether this is a valid PMF and justify both validity conditions explicitly.

steps.title: Check each mass
steps.body: All four values are at least zero.

steps.title: Conclude
steps.body: Both PMF axioms hold, so the proposal is valid.

questions.title: Developing: Normalise a formula
questions.prompt: Let $X$ have support $\{1,2,3,4\}$ and PMF $p_X(x)=cx$. Find the value of $c$ that makes this a valid PMF. Then calculate $P(X\le 2)$.

questions.title: Exam: Build the PMF from outcomes
questions.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled and $X$ is the number of sixes observed. Construct the PMF of $X$, prove that it is valid, and find the probability that at least one six is observed.

questions.title: Foundation: Read a cumulative probability
questions.prompt: A variable has $p_X(0)=0.20$, $p_X(1)=0.50$, and $p_X(2)=0.30$. Find $F_X(1)$ and explain what the value means in words.

steps.title: Interpret
steps.body: There is a 70% probability that $X$ is no larger than 1.

questions.title: Developing: Evaluate between support points
questions.prompt: The support of $X$ is $\{1,3,5\}$ with masses $0.25,0.45,0.30$. Find $F_X(4.8)$ and $P(1<X\le 5)$.

steps.title: Locate 4.8
steps.body: Only support values 1 and 3 are at or below 4.8.

steps.title: Accumulate
steps.body: $F_X(4.8)=0.25+0.45=0.70$. The CDF is flat between 3 and 5.

questions.title: Exam: Recover the PMF from a staircase
questions.prompt: A discrete CDF satisfies $F_X(x)=0$ for $x<0$, $F_X(x)=0.15$ for $0\le  x<1$, $F_X(x)=0.55$ for $1\le  x<3$, and $F_X(x)=1$ for $x\ge3$. Determine the support and the complete PMF.

steps.title: Find the jump locations
steps.body: The CDF changes at $x=0,1,3$, so the support is $\{0,1,3\}$.

questions.title: Foundation: Find a weighted mean
questions.prompt: A game pays $X=0$ pula with probability $0.50$, $X=20$ pula with probability $0.40$, and $X=100$ pula with probability $0.10$. Find the expected payout and explain why the answer is not the most likely payout.

steps.title: Interpret correctly
steps.body: The most likely single payout is 0, but the long-run average over many plays is 18.

questions.title: Developing: Use E[g(X)]
questions.prompt: The number of failed checks in a batch has PMF $p_X(0)=0.5$, $p_X(1)=0.3$, $p_X(2)=0.2$. The repair cost is $g(X)=50+30X^2$ pula. Find the expected repair cost.

questions.title: Exam: Infer a missing mass and then average
questions.prompt: A discrete variable has support $\{-2,0,1,4\}$. Its PMF values are $0.10$, $a$, $0.35$, and $0.20$, respectively. First determine $a$. Then find $E[X]$ and $E[3X-5]$.

questions.title: Foundation: Use the shortcut formula
questions.prompt: A variable has $E[X]=1.1$ and $E[X^2]=1.7$. Find $\operatorname{Var}(X)$ and the standard deviation.

questions.title: Developing: Transform the units
questions.prompt: The daily number $X$ of service calls has $E[X]=12$ and $\operatorname{Var}(X)=9$. A workload score is defined by $Y=2.5X+4$. Find $E[Y]$, $\operatorname{Var}(Y)$, and $\sigma_Y$.

steps.title: Transform the variance
steps.body: $\operatorname{Var}(Y)=(2.5)^2(9)=56.25$. The $+4$ shift does not affect spread.

questions.title: Exam: Find variance from a PMF and then transform
questions.prompt: A game returns $X=-1,2,5$ with probabilities $0.4,0.4,0.2$. Find $E[X]$, $E[X^2]$, and $\operatorname{Var}(X)$. The player’s net score is $Y=-3X+10$. Find $E[Y]$ and $\operatorname{Var}(Y)$.

questions.title: Foundation: Read a joint table and find marginals
questions.prompt: Use the displayed 3-by-3 joint PMF. Find $P(X=2,Y=1)$, $p_X(1)$, $p_Y(0)$, and verify that the table is valid.

steps.title: Read the cell
steps.body: At column $X=2$, row $Y=1$, the cell is $P(X=2,Y=1)=0.10$.

steps.title: Check validity
steps.body: All nine cells are nonnegative and the row totals give $0.40+0.40+0.20=1$.

questions.answer: **Final answer.** $\boxed{P(2,1)=0.10,\ p_X(1)=0.55,\ p_Y(0)=0.40}$; the joint PMF is valid.

questions.title: Developing: Condition on a row and a column
questions.prompt: Using the same table, find $P(X=1\mid Y=0)$ and $P(Y=2\mid X=1)$. Explain why the two denominators differ.

steps.title: Condition on Y=0
steps.body: The given event is a row with total $p_Y(0)=0.40$, so $P(X=1\mid Y=0)=\frac{0.20}{0.40}=0.5$.

steps.title: Condition on X=1
steps.body: The given event is now a column with total $p_X(1)=0.55$, so $P(Y=2\mid X=1)=\frac{0.10}{0.55}=\frac{2}{11}\approx0.1818$.

steps.title: Explain the denominator
steps.body: The denominator is always the probability of what appears after the conditioning bar.

questions.title: Exam: Normalise a joint formula and test independence
questions.prompt: Let $p_{X,Y}(x,y)=c(x+y)$ for $x\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $y\in\{1,2\}$. Find $c$, both marginal PMFs, $P(X=3\mid Y=2)$, determine whether $X$ and $Y$ are independent, and calculate $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)$.

steps.title: Normalise the six weights
steps.body: The weights are $2,3,4$ for $y=1$ and $3,4,5$ for $y=2$; their total is $21$. Hence $c=\frac{1}{21}$.

steps.title: Disprove independence
steps.body: $p(1,1)=\frac{2}{21}$, but $p_X(1)p_Y(1)=\left(\frac{5}{21}\right)\left(\frac{9}{21}\right)=\frac{5}{49}$. The mismatch is enough to conclude dependence.
